pages.text: Today was market day. The village below the hill bustled from early morning.
"The yarn shop is the house with the pointed roof." Mom gave Pipo a basket. "I can buy it myself!" He set off.
At the market entrance, he met Mrs. Goose. "Yarn? They say that shop is best!"
The shop she led him to had mountains of apples. "Oh? Was this not the one?"
She pointed down the next alley. "Then that shop! Everyone says it is good." This one had only pots hanging everywhere.
"The next shop? Or the one beside it?" Mrs. Goose pointed wildly at one after another.
She scratched her head with a wing. "Where did I hear that?"
Pipo stood on tiptoe and looked around. A pointed roof peeped between the others.
The pointed-roof shop was full of yarn. Pipo chose one soft ball.
At home, Mom looked into the basket. "You bought the right thing!" Mrs. Goose came in behind him, still pointing at the roof. Pipo had already put the yarn on Mom's lap.
